paragraphs.source_en: You see, although the microwave radiation is homogeneous across space, if you undertake additional motion beyond that from the cos mic flow of spatial expansion, you will not observe the radiation to be homogeneous. Just as the horn on a speeding car has a higher pitch when approaching and a lower pitch when receding, if you are zipping around in a spaceship, the crests and troughs of the microwaves heading toward the front of your ship will hit at a higher frequency than those traveling toward the back of your ship. Higher-frequency microwaves translate into higher temperatures, so you'd find the radiation in the direction you are heading to be a bit warmer than the radiation reaching you from behind. As it turns out, here on "spaceship" earth, astronomers do find the microwave back ground to be a little warmer in one direction in space and a little colder in the opposite direction.
